cohort: The study included women who underwent either vaginal delivery or cesarean section, with measurements taken during pregnancy, 6 weeks postpartum, and 1 year postpartum.
finding: External anal sphincter EMG amplitude decreased 6 weeks after vaginal deliveries but returned to baseline after 1 year, with no differences observed between vaginal delivery and cesarean section groups after 1 year.
mod_finding: The delivery mode does not have an effect on the EAS amplitude 1 year after delivery, though a slight decrease in sphincter muscle amplitude was noted 6 weeks after vaginal delivery.
